title: per-tenant-slo-feedback-degradation-and-eviction-policy
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce SLO-feedback degradation pipeline: per-tenant degradation profiles, gradual eviction stages, and telemetry. Backwards-compatible config with opt-in policy CR. Improves overall cluster stability under overloaded states by allowing controlled throughput degradation instead of global throttles.
body:
Summary: Adds a new SLO Feedback Controller and Degradation Policy to the Dedicated fleet manager. The controller continuously evaluates per-tenant latency and throughput against tenant SLOs and applies an ordered set of degradation actions (reduced-burst, CPU-prioritized scheduling, soft-evict, hard-evict) with hysteresis and safety timers. The goal is to keep high-priority tenants within their latency SLOs while avoiding large, disruptive fleet-wide throttles during transient pressure.
Motivation: Recent incidents showed that global throttles and blunt eviction policies cause cascading cold-starts and high p95 regressions for latency-sensitive tenants. This PR implements a closed-loop approach: measure -> score -> degrade -> report -> recover. It stitches the degradation actions with the autoscaler and capacity planner so we pre-warm and avoid extended capacity cliffs.
Checklist: - [x] New controller implementation with unit tests - [x] Autoscaler integration (honor degraded tenants' reduced multipliers) - [x] Telemetry and dashboards (per-tenant degradation_level, degradation_reason, prewarm_signals) - [x] Config CRD + default policy - [x] E2E tests simulating load spike and recovery - [x] Documentation and operator notes
Changes (high level): - src/controller/slo_feedback_controller.go: core controller loop, scoring, hysteresis timer, action dispatcher - pkg/autoscaler/policy.go: respect TenantDegradationPolicy when computing target pools - pkg/allocator/evictor.go: soft/hard eviction flow and eviction annotations - charts/dedicated/templates/degradation-policy.yaml: default policy values for installs - docs/operational/degradation-policies.md: operator guide and recovery playbook - test/e2e/degradation_flow_test.go: load spike and recovery scenarios - telemetry/metrics_definitions.md: new metrics and alert recommendations - integrations/capacity-planner/signals.go: prewarm signaling hook
Commits: - 1f4a3b2 Introduce TenantDegradationPolicy CR and default values - 84d2f7b Add SLO Feedback Controller scaffold and main loop - 51c7a90 Implement hysteresis windows and score smoothing - 2c9f8d1 Autoscaler respects degradation multipliers; add tests - 7ab3e35 Evictor: implement soft eviction path (drain pods, mark for prewarm) - 0d2f6b8 Add telemetry tags and dashboards - e5b9a1c E2E tests and flakiness fixes
Files changed (small summary snippets): - src/controller/slo_feedback_controller.go (new, ~420 LOC): core reconcile loop, score computation using p50/p95/throughput/dropped_burst, actionQueue with backoff - pkg/autoscaler/policy.go (mod): added DegradationMultiplier per-tenant, used when computing desiredReplicaWeight - pkg/allocator/evictor.go (mod): softEvict(tenantID, reason) marks instances with annotation "redwood.io/degradation=soft" and drains over 30s; hardEvict takes immediate eviction path - charts/dedicated/templates/degradation-policy.yaml (new): snippet: | TenantDegradationPolicy: default: max_degradation: "soft-evict" p95_threshold_ms: "1200" hysteresis_seconds: "60" - docs/operational/degradation-policies.md (new): operational guidance and suggested alerts (e.g., tenants with degradation_level!=none for >5m)
Design notes and rationale: - Degradation is staged: reduced-burst -> CPU-priority -> soft-evict -> hard-evict. Each stage is reversible and has independent safety timers. - Scoring uses smoothed p95 delta relative to tenant's configured SLO and burst debt as a tiebreaker. Smoothing window defaults to 30s to avoid oscillation on transient spikes. - Hysteresis and minimum-duration timers are critical; we observed in chaos runs that without hysteresis tenants flip states and trigger churn. - Soft-evict marks instances for graceful drain and signals the capacity planner to pre-warm a matching number of warmlets to preserve throughput for non-degraded tenants and to reduce cold-start impact when recovering. - The autoscaler reduces target weights for degraded tenants (configurable multiplier) rather than removing them fully; this prevents headroom starvation for high-priority workloads.
Config example: TenantDegradationPolicy CR (YAML inline example): apiVersion: redwood.io/v1 kind: TenantDegradationPolicy metadata: name: default spec: maxDegradation: soft-evict p95ThresholdMs: 1200 hysteresisSeconds: 60 degradationMultipliers: {"gold": 0.8, "silver": 0.5, "bronze": 0.2}
Metrics added (suggested alerts): - redwood.tenants.degradation_level{tenant_id,level} - redwood.tenants.degradation_duration_seconds - redwood.tenants.degradation_action_count - redwood.tenants.p95_delta - redwood.prewarm.signals_sent
Integration & operator flow: - Controller evaluates metrics via telemetry backend (Prometheus/OTel) and posts actions to allocator API. - During sustained pressure allocator will enact soft-evict for low-priority tenants first; capacity planner receives prewarm signals - Operators can tune the default CR or scope policies per-organization.
Testing: - Unit tests for scoring, hysteresis, and autoscaler interactions added under test/unit - E2E tests simulate 3-tier tenants (gold/silver/bronze) and a spike of 4x baseline traffic. Observed behavior: gold stayed within SLO, silver experienced reduced-burst, bronze soft-evicted then recovered within 4m with prewarm assistance.
Review conversation (excerpt): - Evan Brooks: "Nice approach on the hysteresis windows. Two questions: how do we guarantee prewarm signals are rate-limited?" - Maya Patel: "Prewarm signals are deduped and rate-limited in integrations/capacity-planner/signals.go; added tests to validate dedupe." - Lina Rodriguez: "Please add a note about operator-visible annotations to avoid surprises when debugging evictions." - Maya Patel: "Added annotations and updated docs/operational/degradation-policies.md with troubleshooting section." - Sameer Khatri (approval): "LGTM after telemetry formatting nit."
CI and validation: - CI initially failed flakiness test on e2e; fixes added to stabilize wait durations. - Final CI: all unit, linters, and e2e passed (see checks: unit-tests=pass, linters=pass, e2e=pass, security-scan=pass).
Merge strategy: squash and merge.
Merge commit summary: "Introduce SLO Feedback Controller and TenantDegradationPolicy; staged degradation to protect SLOs and integrate with capacity planner."
Post-merge actions: - Ops: rollout notes published to #oncall and included in release notes. - Observability: dashboard added to "Dedicated Fleet / Tenant Degradation" folder. - Follow-ups: ENG-1602 (add adaptive hysteresis based on request variance), ENG-1620 (audit eviction history per tenant)
Known limitations and future work: - Current scoring depends on tenant-level Prometheus metrics; we'll add optional direct in-process counters for faster feedback (ENG-1602). - Hard-evict still causes short-lived cold starts for recovered tenants; future work adds fast-warm paths. - Policy is opt-in per-install by default; we plan to enable for high-util clusters after ramp.
merge_commit: squash: Introduce SLO Feedback Controller and TenantDegradationPolicy; staged degradation to protect SLOs and integrate with capacity planner
